literal: Gods' even in the world and here obtaining is rare indeed than benevolence good other things.
translation: Even in the world of the gods and in this world, it is rare indeed to obtain other good things better than benevolence.
modern: தேவர் உலகத்திலும் இவ்வுலகத்திலும், ஒப்புரவை விடச் சிறந்த மற்ற நல்லவைகளைப் பெறுவது மிகவும் கடினமாகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of 'oppuravu', which means acting with benevolence and fulfilling one's duty to society. The poet states that finding anything better than this virtue is incredibly rare. He compares 'oppuravu' against all other good things ('nalla piṟa') and concludes it is unmatched. To stress its universal greatness, he notes that this holds true not just 'here' ('īṇṭum') in the human world, but even in the world of the gods ('puttēḷ ulakattum'). Thus, living in harmony with and helping society is presented as the highest possible good.
